title: The Final Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Odile Voss is hired by a dying man, Aurel Kastner, who pays a fortune to prove that his own murder — scheduled for the night his will is read — has not yet happened, so his true heirs can inherit without suspicion falling on them. Digging into a thirty-year-old estate Odile once probated, he discovers Kastner faked his death decades ago and that the 'heirs' are actually conspirators planning a second, final erasure. As the statute of limitations on the original crime expires in nine days, Odile must choose between exposing the conspiracy through legal means and becoming an accessory himself. In the end, Odile uses the will itself as a trap: the document's own clauses force the conspirators to confess on record before they can claim the inheritance, delivering justice outside the courtroom at the cost of Odile's license and his anonymity.
about_author: Vesper Joubert is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's last words before writing her own. She lives near a coastal archive town and claims she has never witnessed a will contested twice by the same family.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Odile Voss, weary estate lawyer, meets Aurel Kastner, who pays triple fees to retain him for a murder that hasn't occurred yet. Kastner insists the crime will be pinned on his heirs unless Odile proves their innocence preemptively. Told partly from Kastner's cryptic POV, the chapter establishes dread beneath civility. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Drafting Kastner's will, he finds it references an earlier estate — one Odile probated thirty years ago under another lawyer's supervision — with clauses that legally cannot coexist. He realizes the old file was sealed improperly, possibly by someone inside his old firm. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your own past is evidence.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs between Odile and retired notary Marguerite Solane, who witnessed the original estate. They reconstruct the night the first Kastner 'died,' finding four alibis so perfectly aligned they must have been rehearsed. Emotional beat: the chill of realizing a lie can be architected like a building.

chapters.title: The Heirs Arrive Early
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The three named heirs descend on the office before the will is even signed, charming and rehearsed, each probing what Odile knows about the old case. One heir, Ilse, slips and mentions a detail only the killer would know. Emotional beat: menace wearing the mask of grief.

chapters.title: What the Statute Forgets
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Researching limitation periods, she and Odile learn the original crime becomes unprosecutable in nine days — meaning someone is racing the clock, and it isn't the police. A break-in at the archive takes the original file. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Erasure
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Kastner reveals fragments of truth: he staged his death thirty years ago to escape the conspirators, and his 'murder' now would let them bury the past forever. But his story contradicts the alibis Marguerite found. Someone is lying — perhaps everyone. Emotional beat: trust curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ilse's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, intimate and unreliable. She corners Odile, offering to trade testimony about the original death for protection from the other heirs. Before she can name names, she vanishes, leaving behind a page torn from the sealed file. Emotional beat: hope arriving one heartbeat too late.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the formal reading, Odile springs his trap: the will's clauses require each heir to orally verify facts of the 1994 estate to inherit. Under oath-adjacent formality, their rehearsed stories fracture against each other in front of witnesses. Emotional beat: controlled terror as the trap closes.

chapters.title: Cipher Broken
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. The heirs realize the verification was recorded; one draws violence into the room, and Kastner — revealed as the architect of both crimes — tries to silence everyone, including Odile. Marguerite's hidden second copy of the file surfaces, and the conspirators' confessions stand. Emotional beat: catharsis bought with blood.

chapters.title: The Price of the Record
chapters.summary: Resolution, Odile's POV. Justice lands outside the law: the bar disbars Odile for his methods, but the recording convicts the guilty and frees Ilse. Kastner, exposed, chooses disappearance over trial, leaving Odile the fee and the truth. Final image: Odile burning his copy of the cipher, finally visible and at peace. Emotional beat: costly, quiet redemption.
